articles.title: Indian national killed as helicopters collide near Mount Everest in Nepal
articles.summary: An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured in a helicopter crash in Nepal.
articles.body: An Indian national was killed and three others, including a New Zealand resident of Indian origin, were injured in a helicopter crash in Nepal. The two helicopters collided while attempting to land near Mount Everest in Nepal on Tuesday morning.The accident took place at around 8.11am (local time) at Pheriche in Ward 4 of Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality in Solukhumbu district.A video of the incident has captured the moment the two aircraft collided, highlighting the dangers of helicopter operations in the busy Everest region.Nepal Police confirmed the casualties from the accident in a statement. They said, "Solukhumbu accident further update: One person dead, three injured"Police identified the deceased as 47-year-old Vasanth Kumar Balaramaramadu, an Indian national travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. His body was taken to a hospital in Lukla.49-year-old Shailesh Krishna Patel, an Indian-origin resident of New Zealand, was also injured who was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter. He was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu by a Prabhu helicopter, police inspector Mausam Tamang said.The other two injured pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty. Both were taken to Kathmandu for further treatment.Who were injured in the collision?Three people were injured in the accident, including two pilots and a passenger.Police inspector Mausam Tamang identified the injured passenger as Shailesh Krishna Patel, a 49-year-old Indian-origin resident of New Zealand. He was travelling aboard the Fishtail Air helicopter along with Balaramaramadu.Patel was airlifted to Mediciti Hospital in Kathmandu for treatment in a Prabhu helicopter, Tamang said.The two injured Nepali pilots were identified as Rabindra Prajapati of Fishtail Air and Prajwal KC of Air Dynasty. Both were taken to Kathmandu for further medical treatment.Who were inside the helicoptersFishtail Air said its helicopter was carrying tourists who had been rescued from the Everest region when it crashed while attempting to land. A company official confirmed that Balaramaramadu and Patel were among the passengers.The Air Dynasty helicopter, meanwhile, was carrying cargo, according to an official from the company.Solukhumbu chief district officer Kaman Singh Thapa Magar confirmed the collision to Reuters and said the injured New Zealand passenger had been rescued.Police have yet to confirm the total number of people aboard the two helicopters at the time of the accident.Where did the accident take place?Pheriche is a settlement along the route to the Mount Everest base camp, around 150 km north-east of Kathmandu. It is an important stop for trekkers and climbers heading towards the world's highest mountain.The collision occurred during Nepal's peak trekking season, when helicopter services are widely used to ferry tourists, mountaineers and rescued trekkers across the Everest region.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. Police said they were collecting further details about the incident.Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) deputy spokesperson Gyanendra Bhul said that the helicopters were approaching the landing area from different directions when the accident occurred, BBC Nepali reported.According to Bhul, one helicopter was travelling from Lukla, while the other was returning from Gorakhpur, near the Everest base camp. Both reportedly attempted to land at the same spot."It appears that the accident occurred when helicopters travelling from Lukla and returning from Gorakhpur, near the base camp, tried to land at the same place," Bhul said.The exact cause of the collision remains unclear. However, preliminary information suggests that snow-covered helipads may have played a role in the accident."It looks like they tried to land on one of the other helipads, perhaps because it was covered in snow, even though there were other helipads," he said.The authorities have not yet released further details about the identities of those involved or the circumstances leading to the collision.You use AI every day. articles.title: Can Trump defy history? The big battles shaping US midterms
articles.summary: The central question in the US midterm elections is whether MAGA supremo Donald Trump can retain control of Congress or whether voters will hand Democrats
articles.body: The central question in the US midterm elections is whether MAGA supremo Donald Trump can retain control of Congress or whether voters will hand Democrats the opportunity to challenge his agenda during the final two years of his presidency.With Americans heading to the polls on Tuesday, all 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the 100 Senate seats are up for grabs. Republicans currently control both chambers, but Trump's falling approval ratings, rising living costs and the war with Iran have given Democrats fresh hope of making gains.According to a BBC report, the elections could determine how much freedom Trump has to push his policies through Congress and how effectively Democrats can challenge his administration.Why midterms matter for TrumpThe midterm elections are traditionally a test of the sitting president's popularity. The party in power often loses seats as voters use the elections to express dissatisfaction with the administration.Trump's approval ratings have added to Republican concerns. According to polling data cited by the BBC, his approval rating began his second term at just over 50% but subsequently fell into the 40s. It dropped below 40% after the US and Israel launched air strikes against Iran at the end of February and currently stands at around 38%.Historically, the president's party has lost an average of 27 House seats in midterm elections since 1934. It has gained seats in only three of the 23 elections held during that period, the BBC reported.The political stakes are particularly high because Republicans have only narrow control of the House. A Democratic takeover of either chamber could make it harder for Trump to advance his legislative agenda.House battle: Republicans face a narrow majorityThe Republicans currently hold 218 seats in the 435-member House of Representatives, giving them a razor-thin majority. All 435 seats are being contested because House members serve two-year terms.However, not every constituency is expected to witness a close contest. According to the Cook Political Report, only 18 seats are considered toss-ups, meaning either party has a realistic chance of winning them.Of these, 14 are currently held by Republicans and four by Democrats. Democrats could also take control by winning seats in constituencies already classified as likely or leaning towards them.The narrow Republican majority means even a relatively small shift in voter support could change control of the House.Senate race: Democrats face a tougher challengeThe battle for the Senate is more complicated for Democrats. Republicans currently hold 53 of the 100 seats, while Democrats have 45. Two independents also vote with the Democrats.Unlike the House, only about one-third of Senate seats are contested every two years because senators serve six-year terms. This time, 35 seats are up for election.The Cook Political Report identifies seven Senate races as toss-ups, six of which are currently held by Republicans. Democrats would need to win four of these seats, along with four seats classified as likely or leaning Democratic, to reach the 51-seat majority.Among the closely watched contests is Michigan, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed faces Republican Mike Rogers, a Trump ally and former FBI agent.Democrats are also targeting traditionally Republican states, including Alaska, Iowa and Ohio. Texas is another key battleground, where Democrat James Talarico is challenging Republican Ken Paxton. A Talarico victory would give Democrats their first Senate seat in the state since 1988, according to the BBC.Cost of living, healthcare and immigration dominate voter concernsThe economy remains one of the biggest challenges for Republicans heading into the elections. Trump had promised to bring down inflation and make everyday life more affordable during his 2024 campaign, but rising costs have remained a major concern for American households.The war with Iran has added to the pressure. Trump had highlighted falling petrol prices in his State of the Union address on February 24, saying prices were below $2.30 per gallon in most states. However, the conflict with Iran began four days later, disrupting energy supplies from the Middle East and pushing petrol prices to around $4 per gallon.The war has also become increasingly unpopular among Americans. A poll conducted in August found that 63% of respondents disapproved of Trump's handling of the conflict, the BBC reported.Healthcare and immigration are other major issues shaping the campaign.Democratic candidates have focused on the rising cost of health insurance and concerns over access to healthcare under Trump's policies. Republicans, meanwhile, have highlighted the administration's immigration measures, with Trump pointing to a sharp fall in illegal border crossings as evidence of their success.Can Trump overcome the political headwinds?Despite the challenges, Republicans have an advantage when it comes to campaign funding.According to figures cited by the BBC, the Republican National Committee and its allied groups had around $320 million in cash reserves in mid-October, compared with just under $230 million for Democrats.Trump's political fundraising group, MAGA Inc, had an additional $160 million or more at its disposal.Republicans have used their financial advantage to step up advertising ahead of the vote. More than $1 billion worth of political advertisements were aired in September, according to research firm AdImpact. Republicans outspent Democrats by around $200 million and had higher advertising expenditure in nearly all closely contested Senate races.The late campaign push is aimed at mobilising Republican voters and limiting potential losses in both chambers.While the overall political environment appears favourable to Democrats, Trump and his party have previously performed better than expected in elections despite unfavourable polling.What happens after the midterms?The outcome will shape the final two years of Trump's presidency. If Democrats take control of either chamber, they could use their position to challenge his policies, scrutinise his administration and make it harder for Republicans to pass legislation.If Republicans retain control of both chambers, Trump will have greater room to pursue his legislative priorities.The elections will also set the stage for the next presidential race in 2028. With Trump constitutionally barred from seeking a third term, political attention is likely to shift towards the next generation of leadership and what Democrats offer voters beyond opposition to the Republican president.You use AI every day. articles.title: 8 arrested for assaulting BSF jawans, snatching service weapon along Tripura border
articles.summary: AGARTALA: Tripura Police arrested eight individuals on Monday night in Sepahijala district for their alleged involvement in the assault on four BSF
articles.body: AGARTALA: Tripura Police arrested eight individuals on Monday night in Sepahijala district for their alleged involvement in the assault on four BSF personnel, including an Assistant Commandant, who were on duty.The incident occurred in the Ashabari region of Boxnagar along the Bangladesh border when the personnel disrupted a smuggling operation the previous afternoon. After learning about the incident, chief minister Dr Manik Saha instructed the Director General of Police to take immediate action against those identified in a widely circulated video.Police teams from Bishalgarh and Kalamchoura police stations launched an extensive search operation and detained all eight primary suspects linked to the attack. A BSF official said the confrontation erupted when a team from the 49th Battalion arrived in response to credible intelligence about suspected smuggling activities.The official said the personnel were unexpectedly attacked by a crowd of villagers, including women and children, who were armed with sticks and sharp weapons during the operation.The group assaulted the jawans and managed to snatch a service weapon from one of them, although it was later recovered. BSF personnel from a nearby area eventually arrived to assist and evacuate the injured troops.The BSF lodged a complaint at Kalamchoura police station, following which an FIR was registered. The charges reportedly include attempt to murder BSF personnel, theft of a weapon and obstructing public officials from performing their lawful duties.Sepahijala SP Bijoy Debbarma said eight individuals had been detained in connection with the attack on BSF personnel in Ashabari. articles.title: A Colorado landowner protected more than 7,400 acres from future development in 2025; the vast ranch remains home to elk, bears and river otters
articles.summary: Scenic Mesa Ranch in Colorado receives permanent protection from development, conserving wildlife habitats and agricultural land for future generations. Discover the importance of conservation easements.
articles.body: In western Colorado, a huge working ranch has received permanent protection from future development. This move has safeguarded the landscape in which agriculture, wildlife and river ecosystems all coexist. The Colorado West Land Trust, in February 2025, announced that owner Peter Slaugh had entered into a partnership with the organisation to conserve Scenic Mesa Ranch, which is a 7,419-acre estate located south of Hotchkiss in the North Fork Valley. Situated close to the confluence of two major waterways, the ranch contains extensive river corridors, canyons, grazing land and wildlife habitats. Therefore, the property’s agricultural legacy and ecological importance are protected by the easement while also allowing permitted ranching activities to continue.Why this 7,400-acre ranch is important for wildlife The location of the Scenic Mesa Ranch is considered strategically important as it is located south of Hotchkiss, stretching along the river corridors upstream from the meeting junction of the North Fork of the Gunnison River and the mainstem of the Gunnison River. According to the Colorado West Land Trust, the region also helps connect lower-elevation public lands with the West Elk Wilderness. The ranch is adjacent to more than 13,000 acres of already conserved land. This conservation easement, therefore, adds to an existing network of protected landscapes.On the other hand, the landscape’s ecological value comes from the variety of environments contained within the boundaries. The vegetated zones alongside rivers and streams fall under its riparian areas and provide habitat for aquatic wildlife and water-dependent bird species. The organisation identifies bald eagles, golden eagles, river otters, elk, mule deer, bighorn sheep, mountain lions and black bears among animals associated with the estate. In addition to that, the ranch contains winter range that elk use, providing forage and cover during colder months. Protecting these various habitats within one estate helps retain the environmental conditions and connections on which wildlife depends.How a conservation easement protects land without completely ending ranchingThrough a conservation easement, the protection of Scenic Mesa Ranch was achieved. In other words, this was a voluntary legal agreement that allows a landowner to retain private ownership while permanently restricting specified development rights. Under this agreement, the Colorado West Land Trust holds the easement and is responsible for enforcing its terms. Usually, these restrictions prevent prohibited subdivision and development, although the exact conditions depend on the individual agreement. He had not originally come to the North Fork Valley to raise cattle or grow crops; instead, he was drawn to the landscapes.One of Slaugh’s concerns was whether his children would be able to retain the entire property eventually. He reportedly said that establishing the conservation easement helped resolve such questions regarding the ranch’s long-term future, as the agreement provides a way to protect the landscape’s conservation values even if it sees a change in ownership in coming years.The next steps for the Scenic Mesa conservation effort will involve improving the conditions of the natural habitats. articles.title: A man claimed a piece of Crown land on St Helena after occupying it for 15 years; the plot was linked to Napoleon Bonaparte's former dairy, and the Privy Council ruled that government land can be acquired through long-term possession
articles.summary: A dispute over a small piece of land on the South Atlantic island of St Helena has brought together an unusual combination of history, property law and a
articles.body: A dispute over a small piece of land on the South Atlantic island of St Helena has brought together an unusual combination of history, property law and a question about the limits of government ownership. The land was associated with a former dairy belonging to Napoleon Bonaparte, who spent the final years of his life in exile on the island. At the centre of the case was a man named Francis, who argued that his long occupation of the plot gave him a legal claim to it. His application raised a question that had not previously been tested in court on St Helena: could someone acquire government-owned land simply by occupying it for 15 years?How Francis used a 15-year possession rule to claim two Crown-owned unitsAccording to The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, the case concerned four industrial units identified as numbers 240, 241, 242 and 249. Francis had entered into a lease with the Governor of St Helena on 25 March 1995, covering units 240 and 242. After taking possession of those premises, he also occupied unit 241. He later took possession of unit 249 in 2006.His claim centred on units 241 and 249, which he said he had occupied for long enough to acquire ownership under the island's land legislation. The relevant provision was section 135 of the Registered Land Ordinance 1980. It allows ownership to pass to someone who has possessed land openly, peacefully and without interruption for 15 years, provided the occupation was without the permission of the person legally entitled to possess it.In July 2023, Francis approached the Registrar of Lands to have the register amended to recognise his claimed ownership. The Crown objected, arguing that government-owned land could not be acquired in this way. The Registrar then referred the legal question to the Supreme Court of St Helena, leaving the individual circumstances of Francis's claim to be considered separately.1833 law that became central to the Crown's land ownership argumentThe Crown's objection rested partly on a provision of the Saint Helena Act 1833, originally the Government of India Act 1833. Section 112 transferred St Helena, along with specified properties and government-related assets on the island, to the Crown.The government also relied on section 159 of the 1980 Registered Land Ordinance. This provision protects interests, rights and powers given to the Crown or government under other written laws. Its argument was that allowing someone to acquire land through 15 years of occupation would interfere with the Crown's rights under the older legislation.Reportedly, a separate constitutional provision, section 31, also featured in the proceedings. It gives the Governor, or someone authorised by the Governor, the power to make grants and other dispositions of Crown property. The government argued that the rules allowing ownership to pass through long-term possession could not override this arrangement.The question was therefore not simply whether Francis had occupied the land for long enough. The courts had to consider how an older law governing the island's transfer to the Crown fitted alongside a much newer system for registering land ownership.The former dairy gave the land its historical connectionFrancis's legal team argued that the disputed land formed part of the former dairy associated with Longwood House, where Napoleon Bonaparte lived during his exile on St Helena from 1815 until his death in 1821.His lawyers referred to a historical map held at the National Archives in London. They argued that it showed the land being used by the East India Company for commercial purposes by 1830, with parts of it leased or intended for sale. If that account was correct, they said, the property might not have fallen within the category of land used for government purposes under section 112 of the 1833 Act.The Crown disputed this interpretation. Its lawyers pointed to New Longwood House, a building constructed between 1818 and 1821 as a possible replacement for Napoleon's original residence. Napoleon never moved into it. According to the government's account, the building subsequently became the residence of Governor Dallas, the last East India Company Governor of St Helena.The Crown cited historical publications referring to Dallas moving into the property in 1832 and a report from 1834 describing the new house as the Governor's residence.The Privy Council did not settle this historical disagreement. It was not necessary to decide whether the disputed property had actually passed into Crown ownership under the 1833 legislation to resolve the principal legal question.The case produced different answers in the island's courtsThe first ruling came from Chief Justice Rupert Jones in the Supreme Court of St Helena in 2024. In Francis v Attorney General of St Helena [2024] SHSC 6, he concluded that there was no legal prohibition on acquiring Crown land through prescription.His reasoning included the distinction between a government grant and a transfer of ownership that occurs through the operation of law. He considered that the constitutional provision governing the Governor's power to dispose of Crown property did not prevent ownership from passing through the statutory possession rules.The Attorney General appealed. Later that year, the Court of Appeal reached a different conclusion in Attorney General of St Helena v Francis [2024] SHCA 5. It agreed that section 31 of the Constitution did not prevent the acquisition of Crown land through prescription. However, it accepted the government's argument about section 159.The appeal court reasoned that, assuming the 1833 Act had vested the disputed property in the Crown, its ownership was protected by the savings provision in the 1980 Ordinance. It therefore answered the Registrar's question in the negative.The land registration system behind the Privy Council's rulingThe appeal was heard on 16 July 2026 by a panel including Lord Reed, Lord Burrows, Lady Rose, Lord Snowden and Sir Anthony Smellie. Lord Reed delivered the judgment on 16 September 2026.A significant part of the Board's reasoning concerned the land registration system established by the 1980 Ordinance. St Helena uses a system based on the Torrens model, under which a public register records ownership and other interests affecting each parcel of land.The system is intended to give people a reliable way of establishing who owns a property without having to reconstruct its entire history through old deeds and records. The register is treated as authoritative, subject to certain interests that the legislation allows to exist without being recorded.The Privy Council considered that the Crown's interpretation of section 159 would undermine this arrangement. If government land could only be acquired through prescription when the Crown had obtained it by a particular means, anyone making such a claim would first have to establish how the government originally acquired the property.The Board also questioned why land acquired by the Crown under an Act of Parliament should receive different treatment from land obtained through a purchase or another route. It found no convincing reason for such a distinction within the legislation.Why the 15-year rule could apply to government landThe Privy Council examined the wording of section 159 alongside the wider provisions of the Ordinance. It accepted that a literal reading might appear to support the government's position. However, it concluded that the provision had to be interpreted in the context of the legislation as a whole.The savings clause was intended to protect statutory rights and powers held by the government, including certain rights to enter, regulate or carry out activities on privately owned land. It was not intended to give the Crown's ownership of land a blanket exemption from the registration system.The distinction mattered because the Ordinance already contained provisions dealing with the registration of Crown property. Section 121, for example, provides for the registration of land to which the Crown becomes entitled under written law or through specified legal procedures.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An Indian seafarer was killed after an Indian-flagged vessel carrying 14 crew members was struck by an unidentified aerial object while
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An Indian seafarer was killed after an Indian-flagged vessel carrying 14 crew members was struck by an unidentified aerial object while navigating near the coast of Oman on Monday, Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal said.The deceased seafarer, identified as Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, succumbed to his injuries, while the remaining 13 crew members were safely evacuated and rescued by the Omani Coast Guard.Sharing details of the incident in a post on X, Sonowal said the vessel, MSV AL JUSUFI, was hit by the unidentified aerial object on November 2."While 13 crew members safely evacuated and were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard, I am deeply saddened to report that one of our seafarers, Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat, tragically succumbed to his injuries," the minister said."He also offered condolences to the deceased's family and said the ministry of ports, shipping and waterways and the Indian Embassy in Oman were in touch with local authorities. The authorities are working to provide immediate assistance to the 13 survivors and facilitate the repatriation of the rescued crew members and the mortal remains of the deceased," Sonowal added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A divorced mother with no restaurant experience, Ruth Fertel mortgaged her New Orleans home in 1965 to buy a 60-seat steakhouse; it became Ruth’s Chris
articles.summary: Discover the remarkable story of Ruth Fertel, a divorced mother who transformed a small New Orleans steakhouse into a world-renowned restaurant chain, Ruth's Chris Steak House, overcoming personal and professional challenges along the way.
articles.body: After her marriage ended in 1958, Ruth Fertel supported her two young sons on her own and later spent four years working at Tulane University Medical School, according to the Horatio Alger Association. In 1965, she purchased Chris Steak House, the restaurant that later became Ruth’s Chris Steak House, the Horatio Alger Association noted. Her salary was not enough to send her sons to college, so she began looking for a way to earn more. Then she noticed an advertisement for a restaurant for sale near the racetrack in New Orleans.She had no restaurant experience and her banker, lawyer, family and friends all advised her not to go ahead, according to the company‘s own history. But she went ahead and bought it, risking her home and turning a little steakhouse on North Broad Street into a household name.The purchase on North Broad StreetEntrepreneur Chris Matulich founded Chris Steak House in New Orleans in 1927 and operated it at 1100 North Broad Street, according to Ruth’s Chris Steak House. In 1965, Ruth Fertel spotted a classified ad for Chris Steak House in the newspaper while looking for a way to pay for her two sons’ education. Despite having no restaurant experience, she mortgaged her home for $22,000, using $18,000 to buy the 60-seat restaurant and the remaining $4,000 for food and supplies, according to Ruth’s Chris Steak House. The restaurant was small. It could accommodate only 60 customers, had no parking and stood near the Fair Grounds Race Course. The area was crowded and the restaurant was struggling even before she took it over. Hurricane Betsy hit New Orleans in September 1965, the same year she bought the restaurant.A dining room run by single mothersOn her first day as owner, Fertel reportedly sold 35 steaks at around $5 each, Mashed reported, citing an archived biography. The dining room was staffed entirely by hard-working, single mothers who later became known as the “Broads on Broad Street", according to the official Ruth’s Chris Steak House website. For many years, it was the only upscale restaurant in New Orleans with an all-female wait staff. In early 1976, shortly after Ruth Fertel signed a new 10-year lease, a kitchen fire destroyed the original Chris Steak House, forcing her to move to a nearby property on Broad Street. Until then, the restaurant had operated under its original name for 11 years. A businessman working in construction agreed to help her and she moved into a bigger restaurant with 160 seats, up from the original 60.Under her contract with Matulich, Fertel could not use the Chris Steak House Name at any other location. So she added her own name in front of the original, creating Ruth’s Chris Steak House. She told Fortune in 1998 that she had always hated the name, but had learnt to live with it, Mental Floss reported.From two restaurants to a global chainFertel worked hard at her New Orleans restaurant and never thought of taking the business beyond the city limits. That changed when a loyal customer who had moved to Baton Rouge kept travelling back to New Orleans for dinner, which prompted her to start franchising, according to Encyclopedia.com.In 1999, Fertel sold a majority stake in the company to Madison Dearborn Partners but kept a minority share. She died in 2002. The firm now has over 150 outlets in operation globally.Why the gamble workedThe restaurant's success came from practical decisions, including the loyal staff, consistent service and stubborn determination to start again after the fire. The little 60-seat steakhouse on North Broad Street has since grown into a worldwide name and the brand still carries the name she was forced to add.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: When treatment exists, no life should be lost because it is unaffordable
articles.summary: There are few things more painful than watching a loved one battle a life-threatening disease.
articles.body: There are few things more painful than watching a loved one battle a life-threatening disease. But perhaps even more heartbreaking is knowing that a treatment exists, and yet a family cannot afford to give its loved one that chance.For such families, the struggle is not only against cancer. It is also against the financial burden of fighting cancer.This is what makes the Government of India's decision to cap trade margins at 30% on 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines so significant. From November 9, the maximum retail prices of some of these medicines are expected to fall by as much as 70%, depending on their existing price structures, with estimated annual savings of ?2,500 crore for patients. It builds on a 2019 intervention covering 42 anti-cancer medicines, which led to price reductions of up to 90% across 526 brands.But the real impact cannot be measured in rupees alone. It must also be measured in families who can continue treatment, and patients who no longer have to choose between their savings and their survival.Cancer does not discriminate between rich and poor. Unfortunately, access to treatment often does.India is at an important juncture. Lifestyle-related diseases are rising, our population is ageing, and cancer is becoming a serious public health challenge. Many patients are still diagnosed at advanced stages, when treatment becomes more complicated, prolonged and expensive.For these patients, medicines are only one part of the financial burden. There are consultations, biopsies, scans, hospitalisation, surgery, chemotherapy, radiation and follow-ups. There is also the cost of travel, staying away from home and income lost during a prolonged illness.According to India's National Health Accounts Estimates for 2022-23, out-of-pocket expenditure accounted for 43.4% of the country's total health expenditure. While this is a significant decline from 64.2% in 2013-14, it highlights how much of the financial responsibility for healthcare continues to rest with Indian households.We must ask ourselves a fundamental question: Should a family lose its lifetime savings simply because one of its members has fallen seriously ill? Surely, as a society, we can do better.India has earned global recognition as the pharmacy of the world, making quality medicines available at competitive prices and benefiting millions of patients across the globe.Our contribution to HIV treatment is a powerful example. Two decades ago, antiretroviral therapy cost thousands of dollars per patient each year. Indian manufacturers helped bring that cost down to less than a dollar a day, making treatment accessible to millions across Africa and Asia.However, we cannot become complacent simply because our medicines are affordable by international standards. Affordability must always be viewed from the perspective of the Indian patient. For a family with a modest income, a medicine that looks inexpensive by global standards may still be beyond reach, especially when treatment continues for months or years.A medicine is not truly affordable because it is cheaper than the same medicine abroad. It is affordable only when the patient who needs it can access it without being pushed into financial hardship.Having spent more than three decades in this industry, I understand that innovation requires substantial investment. Developing new molecules, biological medicines, and advanced therapies involves years of research, scientific uncertainty and significant financial risk. Pharmaceutical companies need sustainable returns to continue investing in the next generation of treatments.But innovation and affordability should never be treated as competing objectives. What is the value of a medical breakthrough if it remains beyond the reach of the very patients it was developed to save?Too often, breakthrough therapies are developed first, and questions of access are addressed much later. Not every therapy can be inexpensive. But affordability should be a design choice, not an afterthought.India has demonstrated its ability to make quality generic medicines accessible at scale. We must now bring the same thinking to complex therapies, biotechnology, diagnostics and next-generation treatments. The future of Indian pharmaceuticals should be built on both scientific excellence and patient affordability.The government's decision also sends a message to every participant in the healthcare value chain: manufacturers, distributors, stockists, retailers, hospitals and healthcare providers. Each must earn enough to sustain operations, maintain quality and invest in better services.The question is not whether businesses should earn profits. Of course they should. The question is whether every layer of the system is creating value proportionate to the cost ultimately borne by the patient.Healthcare is not an ordinary business. When a family is fighting to save a life, it is rarely in a position to negotiate. That places a greater moral responsibility on all of us.A price reduction achieves its purpose only when patients experience the savings at the point of purchase. Revised prices must be reflected in patient bills, and medicines must remain available. Patients and caregivers should also be able to verify revised prices through the NPPA website and the Pharma Sahi Daam app. A medicine that is affordable on paper but unavailable when a patient needs it does little to help.Lower medicine prices are a major step, but India's affordability challenge is much broader. Too many patients delay consultations and diagnostic tests because they fear the cost. By the time a disease is detected, treatment may be longer and more expensive. We must strengthen screening and diagnostics, particularly beyond our major cities.A patient does not experience healthcare as a series of separate bills. They experience it as one continuous treatment journey. Our goal must evolve from making individual medicines affordable to making that entire journey financially sustainable. This will require the government, industry, hospitals and insurers to work together.I sincerely commend the Government of India for this decision. It addresses the difficult balance between commercial interests and public welfare, while placing patient access at the centre.We must continue to build a strong, globally competitive pharmaceutical industry. But we must never forget why this industry exists in the first place.If this policy helps even one more family afford a life-saving treatment, it will have achieved something far more valuable than a reduction in medicine prices.Because ultimately, medical science exists to make treatment possible. Our responsibility is to make it accessible to those who need it.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: How Lawrence Bishnoi gang's social media posts give cops clues to its network, recruits and hideouts
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: When the Lawrence Bishnoi group released a social media screenshot claiming responsibility for the attack on actor Tiger Shroff, to the casual
articles.body: NEW DELHI: When the Lawrence Bishnoi group released a social media screenshot claiming responsibility for the attack on actor Tiger Shroff, to the casual observer, it was just a badge of digital infamy. However, to investigators it was, like always, an opportunity to scan for hidden clues within an open-source intelligence map authored by the criminals themselves.The Lawrence group is considered a pioneer in owning up to crimes through online press releases. Abandoning the underworld's traditional code of secrecy, the gang weaponised performative violence, broadcasting screenshots within an hour of a hit. At times, they are accompanied by point-of-view videos of the shootings too.When the syndicate posts these cyber-manifestoes following a high-profile strike, it offers an unfiltered window into the inner workings of the gang, officials say. In the Mumbai case, for example, it provided the cops many leads to start with. It mentioned three names -- Anmol Bishnoi, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. It had a hashtag of a Delhi-based gang, "Gogi-Maan group". Incidentally, in the next few days, multiple arrests were made in the case from the two places as cops followed up with the leads on Anil Pandit's network. The gang also claimed that Tiger ignored warnings, prompting cops to to dig in to the call and IP records besides recee angles.Sometimes, the posts introduce new gang members too. A screenshot released last year, for instance, mentioned a mysterious name, Tyson Bishnoi, whose actual identity continues to be a mystery. Aarzoo Bishnoi was another such member introduced through posts. Beyond announcements, these uploads also double as digital press releases for internal promotions, newly forged alliances, or brewing rivalries through hashtags. "These are meticulously curated propaganda tool machines where every name and hashtag holds a tip. The names, for example, expose the possible locations of key henchmen who use location-tagged monikers as digital status symbols," said an investigator.Anil Pandit branded himself as 'Anil Pandit USA' on social media to lure impressionable young recruits with the "American dream". Lately, however, the 'USA' suffix has mysteriously vanished from his profile handle, prompting investigators to wonder if the shift stems from pressure exerted by the FBI's Operation Hardball or indicates an evasion tactic as he changes hideouts. Many others embed their geographical jurisdiction directly into their handles - Fateh Portugal, Sam Canada, Manna Brampton, Mandy Spain, and X Australia are a few cases in point. Beyond serving as intelligence goldmines, these posts fulfil a psychological purpose, operating as digital shrines of friendship and loyalty tailored specifically for Gen Z recruits.
